events.title: Jeremiah's Call
events.description: God calls Jeremiah to be a prophet and says he was known and set apart before he was born. Jeremiah protests, saying he is too young, but God touches his mouth and puts His words in it. God shows him two visions: an almond branch as a sign that God watches over His word, and a boiling pot turning from the north as a sign of coming judgment on Judah. Jeremiah is told to proclaim against the whole land, and God promises to be with him.

events.title: The Broken Covenant Relationship
events.description: God sends Jeremiah to proclaim to the people in Jerusalem that they have abandoned him, the source of living water, and instead have hewn out broken cisterns that cannot hold water. Israel has traded their glory for idols and done double evil. Jeremiah urges the people to repent and describes their apostasy as unfaithfulness toward God.

events.title: The Enemy from the North
events.description: Jeremiah prophesies about an enemy coming from the north who will lay the land waste. The trumpet sounds, and disaster approaches from Dan. The people are urged to put on sackcloth and mourn, for the Lord's burning anger has not turned away from them. Jeremiah depicts the destruction with vivid imagery and laments the hardness of the people's hearts.

events.title: The Temple Sermon
events.description: God sends Jeremiah to stand at the temple gate and preach to all who come to worship. He warns them against trusting in false words: The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord! Jeremiah points to Shiloh, where God's dwelling first stood, which was destroyed because of the people's sin. If they do not repent, God will do the same to this temple and reject them.

events.title: The Broken Jar
events.description: God tells Jeremiah to buy a clay jar and take some of the elders of the people and the priests to the Valley of Hinnom. There he proclaims judgment against Jerusalem because the people have abandoned God, sacrificed to foreign gods, and burned their sons as offerings to Baal. Jeremiah shatters the jar in front of the witnesses and says that just like this jar, God will break this people and this city so that it cannot be made whole again.

events.title: The Potter's Workshop
events.description: God sends Jeremiah down to the potter's workshop to hear his word. Jeremiah sees that when a vessel is ruined in the potter's hands, he reshapes it into another vessel as he pleases. God explains that He is like this potter toward Israel: He can change His mind about judgment if the people repent, and change His mind about blessing if they do evil. This is a powerful image of God's sovereignty and human responsibility.

events.title: Jeremiah in the Stocks
events.description: The priest Pashhur, son of Immer and chief officer in the temple, hears Jeremiah's prophecies, strikes him, and puts him in the stocks at the Benjamin Gate of the temple. The next day, when Pashhur releases him, Jeremiah gives him the name Magor-Missabib (Terror on Every Side) and prophesies that Pashhur and all his household will be taken captive to Babylon. After this, Jeremiah expresses deep anguish and curses the day he was born.

events.title: The Message to King Zedekiah
events.description: King Zedekiah sends messengers to Jeremiah to inquire of the Lord when Nebuchadnezzar lays siege to Jerusalem. Jeremiah answers that God himself will fight against Judah with outstretched hand and strong arm. The people are given a choice: those who remain in the city shall die by sword, famine, and plague, but those who go out to the Chaldeans shall save their lives. Jeremiah urges the royal house to practice justice and righteousness, or God's wrath will flare up like an unquenchable fire.

events.title: The Good and Bad Figs
events.description: After King Jeconiah and the leading figures of Judah are taken into exile in Babylon, God shows Jeremiah two baskets of figs before the Lord's temple. One basket contains very good figs, the other very bad. God explains that the good figs represent those exiled to Babylon, whom he will watch over, bring back, and rebuild. The bad figs represent King Zedekiah and those remaining in Jerusalem, whom he will hand over to destruction, sword, famine, and plague.

events.title: The Prophecy of Seventy Years of Exile
events.description: Jeremiah proclaims that because the people have not listened to God's prophets, God will send Nebuchadnezzar against this land and make it a desolate wasteland. The nations shall serve the king of Babylon for seventy years. But when the seventy years are completed, God will punish the king of Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans and make it an everlasting desolation. This prophecy became central to the hope of the exiles and was later referenced by Daniel.

events.title: Jeremiah and Hananiah
events.description: The prophet Hananiah from Gibeon stands up in the temple and proclaims that God will break the yoke of the king of Babylon within two years and bring back the exiles and the temple vessels. Jeremiah wears a wooden yoke on his neck as a sign of Babylon's dominion, and Hananiah breaks it off. Jeremiah goes on his way, but God sends him back with the message: You have broken a yoke of wood, but in its place you will get a yoke of iron. Jeremiah prophesies that Hananiah shall die within the year because he has preached rebellion against the Lord, and Hananiah dies two months later.

events.title: The Letter to the Exiles
events.description: Jeremiah sends a letter from Jerusalem to the elders, priests, prophets and all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had taken into exile in Babylon. He urges them to build houses, plant gardens, take wives and seek the welfare of the city where they have been exiled, for in its peace you will find your own peace. The letter contains a promise that after seventy years God will turn his attention to them, fulfill his good word and bring them back. The well-known verse reads: I know the plans I have for you, declares the Lord, plans for welfare and not for evil, to give you a future and a hope.

events.title: The New Covenant
events.description: In the midst of the Book of Consolation, Jeremiah proclaims God's promise of a new covenant with the house of Israel and Judah. This covenant will be different from the one God made with their ancestors when He brought them out of Egypt, the covenant they broke. In this new covenant, God will put His law within them and write it on their hearts. All will know the Lord, from the least to the greatest, for God will forgive their guilt and remember their sin no more. This is one of the most central prophecies in the Old Testament, which the New Testament directly links to Jesus' work of salvation.

events.title: Jeremiah Buys a Field in Anathoth
events.description:
While Jerusalem is besieged by the Babylonians and Jeremiah sits imprisoned in the guard court, God commands him to buy a field in Anathoth from his cousin Hanamel.  
Jeremiah carries out the purchase with witnesses, weighs out the silver, and seals the deed.  
He gives the documents to Baruch with instructions to put them in an earthenware jar so they can be preserved for a long time.  
This act is a prophetic sign that one day houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land, despite the impending destruction.

events.title: The Scroll Is Burned by Jehoiakim
events.description: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim's reign, God commands Jeremiah to write all his prophecies on a scroll. Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe, reads the scroll aloud in the temple before the people. The princes hear about it and ask Baruch to read to them as well. They become afraid and bring the scroll to the king. King Jehoiakim sits by the winter fire, and as three or four columns are read, he cuts them off with a scribe's knife and throws them into the fire until the entire scroll is burned. He shows no fear and refuses to repent. God commands Jeremiah to write a new scroll with even more words than the first, and prophesies judgment against Jehoiakim.

events.title: Jeremiah Is Imprisoned
events.description: During the siege of Jerusalem, Jeremiah tries to leave the city through the Benjamin Gate to receive his inheritance in the land of Benjamin. The guard commander Irijah arrests him and accuses him of intending to defect to the Chaldeans. Jeremiah denies this, but the officials become furious, beat him, and put him in the prison at the house of the scribe Jonathan. He remains there for many days until King Zedekiah secretly brings him out and asks if there is a word from the Lord. Jeremiah answers that the king will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and asks to return to the prison. The king transfers him to the guard court.

events.title: Jeremiah Is Thrown into a Cistern
events.description:
The princes accuse Jeremiah of undermining the morale of the war because he says that whoever stays in the city will die, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live.  
They get King Zedekiah’s permission and throw Jeremiah down into Malkijah’s cistern in the guard court, where there is no water but only mud, and Jeremiah sinks into the mud.  

Ebed-Melech, an Ethiopian official, goes to the king and says that the men have acted wickedly.  
The king gives orders to pull Jeremiah up, and Ebed-Melech gets old rags and cloths which he lowers down to Jeremiah so that the ropes will not cut him.  
In this way Jeremiah is rescued from the cistern.

events.title: The Fall of Jerusalem
events.description: In the eleventh year of Zedekiah's reign, on the ninth day of the fourth month, the Babylonians break through the city wall after a siege of one and a half years. King Zedekiah flees at night through the king's garden, but the Chaldeans pursue him and capture him in the plains of Jericho. Nebuchadnezzar holds judgment over him at Ribla: Zedekiah's sons are killed before his eyes, then his own eyes are put out, and he is taken in chains to Babylon. The Babylonians burn the temple, the king's house, and all the great houses in Jerusalem, and tear down the city walls. Jeremiah is released by Nebuchadnezzar's command and allowed to choose whether to stay in the land.

events.title: Gedaliah Murdered
events.description: Nebuchadnezzar appoints Gedaliah as governor over those remaining in Judah. Gedaliah settles in Mizpah and urges the people to serve the king of Babylon and cultivate the land. Ishmael, son of Nethaniah and of royal descent, comes to Mizpah with ten men and kills Gedaliah along with the Judeans and Chaldeans who are with him. He also kills a group of pilgrims from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. Johanan and the other commanders pursue Ishmael and rescue those taken captive at the great waters of Gibeon, but Ishmael himself escapes to the Ammonites.

events.title: Jeremiah Taken to Egypt
events.description: Johanan and all the commanders ask Jeremiah for advice and swear to obey God's word. After ten days the word of the Lord comes to Jeremiah: Stay in the land, so that God will build you up and not tear you down. You must not fear the king of Babylon. But if you go to Egypt, sword, famine, and plague will strike you there. The people refuse to listen and accuse Baruch of stirring up Jeremiah against them. They take the whole remnant with them, including Jeremiah and Baruch, and go to Tahpanhes in Egypt. There Jeremiah prophesies that Nebuchadnezzar will also come to Egypt.

events.title: Oracle Against Egypt
events.description: The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah concerning Egypt and Pharaoh Necho's army, which was defeated at Carchemish by Nebuchadnezzar. The prophecy describes Egypt's warriors preparing for battle, only to be struck with panic and flee. Egypt's fall is compared to the rising flood of the Nile, but the Lord, God of hosts, takes vengeance on his enemies. Jeremiah also proclaims that Nebuchadnezzar will come and strike Egypt, yet eventually the land will be inhabited again.

events.title: Oracle against Babylon
events.description: Jeremiah pronounces a long prophecy against Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans. A people from the north shall come and make the land a desolation. Israel and Judah shall seek the Lord and inquire for the way to Zion. Babylon, which was God's instrument to punish the nations, shall itself be punished for its own guilt. The walls shall be torn down, the temples destroyed, and the land shall become an eternal desolation. Jeremiah writes all these words in a scroll and gives it to Seraiah with the command to read it aloud in Babylon, then tie a stone to it and cast it into the Euphrates as a sign that Babylon shall sink and never rise again.

events.title: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile of Judah
events.description: The last chapter repeats the account of Jerusalem's fall. Zedekiah rebels against Babylon, and the city is besieged for two years. When the famine becomes too severe, the king flees but is captured and judged in Ribla. Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, burns the temple, the king’s palace, and all significant buildings. The walls are torn down, and the people are taken away. The chapter ends by mentioning three deportations and the total number exiled. Finally, it is reported that King Jehoiachin is released from prison in Babylon by Evil-Merodach and eats at the king's table for the rest of his days.
